bull.b: Extremely low leverage and a substantially strengthened capital base provide financial flexibility for clinical development. This reduces near-term balance-sheet stress, although the company remains dependent on capital because it has not yet generated revenue.

Broader licensed rights increase the potential strategic and commercial scope of ORKA-001 across multiple use cases. This may improve future partnering flexibility and supports development of a more valuable long-term product franchise.

Strong shareholder support for directors, independent audit oversight and executive compensation indicates continuity in governance. A stable mandate can help management execute clinical and operational priorities without evident organized shareholder opposition.

bear.b: With no current revenue, Oruka lacks internally generated funding and remains reliant on its pipeline, financing or future partnerships. The business therefore carries substantial development and commercialization risk until clinical assets produce recurring cash inflows.

Expanding net and operating losses show that spending is rising ahead of commercialization. Unless development progress leads to revenue, licensing income or another funding source, persistent losses will continue to pressure capital efficiency and shareholder funding needs.

The worsening cash-flow deficit increases dependence on future financing or partnering proceeds to sustain clinical programs. Although the burn broadly tracks net loss, the trajectory could reduce financial flexibility and increase dilution or funding risk over time.
